slides.title: General challenges
slides.content: General challenges Ambiguity Types of ambiguity • Lexical: I saw a bat saw = past tense of see or present tense of saw bat = ﬂying mammal or wooden club • Structural: I saw a man with a telescope I have a telescope or the man does • Semantic: John and Mary are married to each other or to other people • Anaphoric: Margaret invited Susan, and she gave her a sandwich. she = Margaret or Susan 15 NLP: Introduction

slides.title: Representing words and sentences
slides.content: Representing words and sentences Representing words Vocabulary: {sky, wings, engine, helicopter, drone, rocket, goose, eagle, bee} The goose is in the sky. The eagle in the sky has wings. The bee in the sky has wings. The goose with wings in the sky. The eagle with wings in the sky. The bee with wings in the sky. The goose and the eagle with wings are in the sky. The goose flies in the sky. The wings of the bee are good wings. The helicopter, the drone and the rocket are in the sky. The helicopter in the sky is a useful engine. The drone in the sky is an engine that takes pictures. A rocket is an engine. The helicopter is an engine. A drone is an engine that takes pictures. A rocket is a useful engine among sky engines. A helicopter is flying in the sky. The sky is full of helicopters and drones. The engine here is a drone, the one there is a rocket. Toy corpus 22 NLP: Introduction

slides.title: Course overview
slides.content: Course overview Course overview Linguistic structures: Why bother? • POS tagging, dependency parsing, etc. are currently not used in production. But: • LLMs are black boxes • Understanding the challenges in processing language is crucial to interpretability • It can help identifying weaknesses and analysing errors • LLMs do not work well for low-resource languages • These tasks may still have relevance for these languages • LLMs have massive amounts of parameters • More sustainable models may involve these tasks 40 NLP: Introduction

slides.title: Practical information
slides.content: Practical information Views on teaching Views • Traditional lectures are bad - you learn best by activating your brain . • Interaction with teacher and peers boosts learning - you should feel encouraged to come to class. • You should not feel obliged to come (stay home if you are sick!) • The belgian system where you do everything during the "blok" is bad, learning takes time 42 NLP: Introduction

slides.title: Practical information
slides.content: Practical information Course format Course content • All content material is online on the Toledo platform: • Pre-recorded videos of the lectures • Slides • Required readings • In-class exercises and solutions • Labs and solutions • Slides (lectures/videos): high-level intuitive explanations • Required readings: necessary to understand the models and algorithms in detail 43 NLP: Introduction

slides.title: Practical information
slides.content: Practical information Relation to other courses this academic year It is complementary to the Computational Linguistics course taught by Tim Van de Cruys (not a requirement). Computational Linguistics Stronger focus on the linguistic formalisms and high-level intuitions of models. NLP We go deeper in mathematical modelling and see the diﬀerent algorithms in more detail. We are collaborating to make the courses as compatible as possible. Redundancy may still happen. We welcome feedback! 46 NLP: Introduction

slides.title: Practical information
slides.content: Practical information Relation to other courses this academic year Advanced NLP taught by Pieter Delobelle. • For MirAI students • Large content overlap in the lectures + project • In Dutch 47 NLP: Introduction

slides.title: Practical information
slides.content: Practical information Evaluation Open-book written exam Focus on understanding rather than memorizing. Exam • Theoretical part (50%): Broad overview questions, comparison of technologies, explaining algorithms. • Exercise part (50%): Apply algorithms or evaluation metrics and analyse the results. Analyse the output of programs used in the labs. Information sheet with example questions will be made available on toledo mid-October 48 NLP: Introduction
